newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists oppose sale of Telecom.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists oppose sale of Telecom.

text.p: The Socialists oppose privatisation of state-owned France Telecom and believe the government should retain 100 percent ownership of the telecommunications giant, party spokesman Francois Hollande said in a newspaper interview.

The Socialist party, which polls indicate is gaining ground on the ruling centre-right party in the run-up to the May/June parliamentary election, is against "privatising even partially, France Telecom, because that would mean abandoning the principles of public service," he told business daily La Tribune.
"For those public services -- France Telecom, the Post Office, (power utility) EDF-GDF and of course (railway) SNCF -- our position is to keep public ownership at 100 percent," he said.
The conservative government has suspended plans to sell off some 30 to 35 percent of France Telecom until after the elections are over.

Hollande said that the Socialists did not rule out privatising companies which did not have any public service mandate, saying that realism should be the ruling principle in government choices of which firms to sell.
"We need to keep a certain flexibility, what we call breathing room," he said.
"For companies in which the capital is already open and in which the state's holding is no more than symbolic, there are no obstacles (to privatisation)," he added.

He also reiterated the party's opposition to privatisation of state-owned defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF. He said it could "remain an independent company -- it could also be linked to Dassault -Aerospatiale."
"Public ownership does not prevent exploiting synergies or forming industrial alliances."
"In the defence industry," he added, "we plan to maintain public control."
